adversarial_reasoning.location: reports/current.md:1-386; three workload models, fixed-input sensitivity, self-hosting crossover and value-chain sections
adversarial_reasoning.basis: Read the complete task and complete 386-line report. Challenged the cheap-token-to-cheap-task inference, assumed failure detection, retry dependence, ignored unresolved work, labor opportunity cost versus cash saving, cache expiry, model-quality substitution and self-hosting feasibility. Inspected retained originals TE13 sections 5.6 and 6.8-6.9 (lines 364-379,565-570), DistServe TE12 experimental and fault-tolerance limits (307-319,265-267), and the existing calculation-results hosting and derived_checks entries without rerunning them. The report correctly rejects output-only API comparisons and co-tenant cost as universal procurement evidence; its own capacity/quality values are explicit scenarios and impossible one-node crossovers remain infeasible. The output sensitivity explicitly holds downstream history fixed and disclaims full-history interpretation. Each cohort counts failed and unresolved work, quality/routing conditions are not claimed as measured named-model performance, and value/margin claims retain their denominator. No necessary adversarial-reasoning defect found.
